About the School of Architecture, Computing and Engineering (ACE)

The School of Architecture, Computing and Engineering (ACE) is a dynamic and multidisciplinary school bringing together expertise across engineering, computing, architecture and the built environment. Through its research groups and close collaboration with the Sustainability Research Institute, ACE is committed to delivering innovative, impact-led research that addresses some of society’s most pressing challenges.

This role sits within the Department of Engineering and Construction and offers the opportunity to contribute to world-leading research focused on energy systems, decarbonisation and the transition to net zero. Working closely with academic partners at Imperial College London and industry stakeholders, you will join a thriving research environment dedicated to developing practical solutions that support sustainable communities and smarter energy networks.

About the Job

We are seeking an outstanding Research Associate to join a UKRI-funded research project, Behavioural Data-Driven Coalitional Control for Buildings. Based at our Docklands Campus, you will work alongside researchers at the University of East London and Imperial College London to develop innovative distributed optimisation and data-driven control solutions for groups of buildings and energy systems.

This exciting 18-month fixed-term opportunity will contribute to cutting-edge research that helps address one of the defining challenges of our time: climate change mitigation and the transition to a net-zero future.

Key responsibilities include:

Developing optimisation algorithms and distributed control strategies for building energy systems.
Conducting research into data-driven methodologies and predictive control approaches.
Publishing high-quality research outputs in leading international journals and conferences.
Presenting findings to academic, industrial and project stakeholders.
Collaborating with researchers at Imperial College London and industry partners including UK Power Networks and SSE Energy Solutions.
Contributing to project deliverables, technical reports and dissemination activities.

Informal enquiries may be addressed to Dr Paola Falugi at p.falugi@uel.ac.uk

About You

You will hold a PhD in a discipline involving optimisation and data-driven methodologies and have a strong track record in research, problem-solving and analytical thinking.

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

Experience developing optimisation algorithms and distributed optimisation techniques.
Knowledge of control engineering and predictive control methodologies.
Strong programming and computational skills.
A background and experience in control engineering and predictive control strategies under uncertainty.
Experience applying data-driven approaches to complex engineering problems.
The ability to communicate effectively with academic and industrial stakeholders.
A proactive and collaborative approach, with the ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
A commitment to producing high-quality research publications and impactful outcomes.

Experience in building modelling, energy systems modelling and machine learning techniques would be advantageous.

The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more.

Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

 

Overview

 

Turning validated plant science into an investable product demands dedicated commercial leadership. The BBSRC Follow-on Fund project ‘Vaccines for Plants: Advanced Immunity for Residue-Free Crops’ aims to develop a crop-protection platform that combines induced resistance (IR) agents with synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) for protected lettuce and tomato. Reporting to Professor Jurriaan Ton in the School of Biosciences, you will lead the project’s commercialisation and knowledge.

 

Regulatory guidelines, intellectual property (IP) and market evidence will determine the platform’s value as much as efficacy data. The project commits to engaging the Health and Safety Executive (HSE) from month one, planning and submitting an Administrative Trials Permit (ATP) application by month 6, filing patents by month 12 and assembling an investable evidence package by the end of the project. You will drive this programme, acting as principal contact for our consultant, Capital Agri, and linking the research team, the University’s Commercialisation Team, industry partners and growers.

 

The role is suited either for people with previous experience in translational plant research, including application of basic scientific research to commercial products, or a professional form the agricultural sector with sound education in plant biology and/or plant pathology. You will combine knowledge about plant pathology or crop protection with an understanding of IP, market research and stakeholder engagement. In return, you will help shape a planned University spin-out that offers UK growers a residue-free alternative to chemical fungicides.

 

Applicants must hold a PhD (or be close to completion / have equivalent postdoctoral work experience) in plant science, plant pathology, microbiology, agricultural science or a related subject. Experience in translational crop research on plant–microbe interactions or crop protection in research institutions (Universities or Research institutes) or R&D units of the commercial agricultural/horticultural/crop protection sector is also essential.

Lead the project’s commercialisation and knowledge exchange work.

Act as principal contact for the project’s commercial consultant.

Conduct market research and customer discovery (with assistance from consultant).

Coordinate the regulatory pathway with the HSE.

Write periodic (once per year) project reports to update project stakeholders

Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post

About the Role  

About the Role

We are seeking a Postdoctoral Research Associate to join a Barts Charity-funded project investigating early-onset type 2 diabetes and mid-life frailty in British Bangladeshi and British Pakistani communities in East London.
The postholder will analyse longitudinal data from the Genes & Health study, including linked NHS health records and genomic data. They will prepare analysis-ready datasets, derive and validate frailty measures, undertake longitudinal statistical analyses, and examine associations with hospitalisation, falls, cardiovascular events and mortality.

The role will also contribute to peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, patient and public involvement activities, project reporting and the development of reproducible analytical pipelines. About You You will have a PhD, or be close to completion, in epidemiology, health data science, statistics, bioinformatics or a related quantitative discipline.

You will have strong practical experience of managing and analysing large-scale longitudinal health data using R, together with knowledge of epidemiological research methods and reproducible analytical practice. You should be able to work independently, manage priorities and communicate findings clearly to academic, clinical and non-specialist audiences.

Experience of linked NHS electronic health records, secure research environments, longitudinal modelling, frailty, diabetes, genomic data or polygenic risk scores would be advantageous.

About the School/Department/Institute/Project

The post will be based in the Centre for Primary Care within the Wolfson Institute of Population Health.

The project brings together expertise in epidemiology, diabetes, healthy ageing, genomics and population health. Using the Genes & Health cohort, it will investigate whether younger onset type 2 diabetes is associated with an increased burden and faster progression of frailty in mid-life.

The project addresses an important health inequality affecting East London’s South Asian communities and will generate methods and preliminary evidence to support future research, earlier risk identification and improved service planning. Throughout our history, we’ve fostered social justice and improved lives through academic excellence. And we continue to live and breathe this spirit today, not because it’s simply ‘the right thing to do’ but for what it helps us achieve and the intellectual brilliance it delivers.

We continue to embrace diversity of thought and opinion in everything we do, in the belief that when views collide, disciplines interact, and perspectives intersect, truly original thought takes form.

About the role

The Post-doctoral Research Fellow (PDRF) will contribute to activities associated with the project “Governing novel conservation and ecological engineering through plural value frames and systemic risk assessment”, joining a team at the Universities of Reading and Sussex and the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. This exciting project is funded by ARIA, the UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency, as part of a programme on Accelerated Adaptation (within the Resilient Climate and Ecosystems opportunity space). 

The project aims to embed a holistic governance approach across the entire programme, engaging communities, developing nature-centric governance approaches that treat nature itself as a stakeholder rather than simply a resource to manage, and assessing systemic risks that novel interventions could introduce, from unintended ecological harm to eroded public trust. The role will focus on the regulation and systemic risk assessment of such technological advances, acknowledging the plural values around these and other approaches to nature restoration. The successful candidate will work with colleagues to plan and deliver enhanced systemic risk assessments of six primary research projects in the ARIA “Accelerating Adaptation” programme. They will help to develop a risk register encompassing the range of environmental and social/ socio-technical risks, co-identified with project teams. The role involves developing transdisciplinary methodologies and working with domain experts in novel conservation and ecological engineering projects such as treatment of trees against bacterial infection, genetic engineering of bacteria to defend amphibians against fungal diseases, seed priming to engineer early drought-tolerance in trees and exploring whether the resilience of pollinators can be enhanced. 

This role will require working with other team members, scientists in the ARIA programme and a range of stakeholders. You will work under the direction of Adrian Ely, Professor of Technology and Sustainability in collaboration with the wider team at Sussex (Dr Joanna Smallwood), Reading (Marzia Briel and Prof Tom Oliver),  Royal Botanic Gardens, Edinburgh (Alexandra Davey) and GLIC community and economy consultants. You will collaborate closely with another post-doctoral researcher who will be hired in parallel at Reading to focus on bringing a Rights of Nature lens to the governance of the approaches being pioneered in the programme.

About you

You will have a PhD or equivalent experience in environmental risk assessment or regulation and governance of biotechnology (including synthetic biology or engineering biology), in particular its application to biodiversity conservation. Familiar with theories, literature and debates around responsible innovation and nature restoration, you will have a deep commitment to social and environmental justice, and an ambition to use your research to bring about change in the world. You will have experience of working across different disciplines (e.g. with legal scholars and natural scientists) and also with partners outside academia. You will have the skills to manage your own workload, motivating yourself and at times supporting other colleagues. You will have good inter-personal skills and be able to communicate clearly with the team, line management, and stakeholders. You will ideally be able to work at the University of Sussex three days per week, and be willing to undertake some national and international travel associated with the position.

About our School

As a pioneering research-driven and interdisciplinary Faculty, the University of Sussex Business School offers an inspiring and supportive environment for impactful business and management research and scholarship. Our five dynamic Departments—Accounting and Finance, Strategy and Marketing, Management, Economics, and the renowned Science Policy Research Unit (SPRU)—are dedicated to advancing academic excellence and practical insights to inform policy and drive responsible business solutions.

With a strong commitment to innovation and sustainability, the School shapes the future of business education, producing research and scholarship and graduates that make a difference in the UK and globally. By joining us, you will be part of a distinctive, future-focused community influencing real-world practices and promoting sustainable development.

Senior Research Associate (Research Culture)

The role

We are seeking a part-time Senior Research Associate to lead the research activities looking at how initiatives focused on research culture lead to positive and sustained changes in behaviour, practices, processes and values.

The role is based in Research and Innovation Services, but will work closely with the Associate Pro Vice-Chancellor for Research Environment and Culture Daniela Schmidt and Research Culture Strategy Manager Yasmine Rhoseyn.

What will you be doing?

Research culture refers to the values, expectations, behaviours and processes that shape how we support, deliver and communicate research.

This post will play a key role in understanding how research culture change happens in practice, by researching how research culture initiatives have been devised and led across Bristol, and unpicking through qualitative methodologies the conditions that need to be present in order for change to occur. This could also include identifying any unintended outcomes resulting from change, and the barriers that impede the progress of successful change.

This is an exciting research opportunity in an emerging and evolving area that has the ability to help generate real impact.

You should apply if

You have:

Experience in qualitative research methodologies (case studies, interviews, focus groups)
An interest in research culture, evaluation and/or change management
A PhD or near completion, or equivalent research experience in an academic, industrial or clinical setting equivalent to a PhD

We welcome and encourage applications from colleagues with both an academic background or professional or industry background so long as you meet the essential criteria.

Hybrid working is avaiable with one day per week on campus.

The role

We are seeking to appoint a highly motivated and experienced Senior Research Associate for a 2.5-year position to work on extreme drought as part of the UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship ‘Projecting extreme droughts in rapidly changing human-water systems’. The role will focus on assessing the resilience of water systems across Great Britain, with scope for a range of topics to be covered including:

Projecting future streamflow droughts across Great Britain
Assessing the resilience of river flows to changes in water supply
Exploring human impacts on drought propagation through the terrestrial water cycle
Co-developing management scenarios to explore adaptation options to future droughts
Modelling multi-purpose reservoirs

This post presents an exciting opportunity to work on a global water challenge with an energetic interdisciplinary team and high potential for impact. There will be a strong focus on career development for the successful candidate with opportunities and funding available to undertake relevant training/development activities, pursue your own research interests, write fellowship applications, go on placements with project partners and international research conferences and visits.

Supervise and support early career colleagues and PhD students where appropriate.

A PhD in hydrology or equivalent hydrological research experience in an academic or industrial setting
Substantial research experience of hydrological/water systems data analysis and modellingacross large samples of catchments
Strong analytical and coding skills within a package such as MATLAB, R or Python.  
Evidence of peer-reviewed publications in high-quality journals

Senior Research Associate in Mammalian Jaw Development
 Apply
The role

We are seeking a two-year postdoctoral research assistant (Senior Research Associate) at the University of Bristol, UK, in collaboration with King’s College London. The successful candidate will undertake research into the development and mechanobiology of the mammalian jaw. The post is funded by an ERC Advanced Grant awarded to Professor Emily Rayfield at the University of Bristol, in collaboration with Professor Abigail Tucker in the Centre for Craniofacial and Regenerative Biology

at King’s College London.

 

The aim of the project is to test the effect of diet hardness on postnatal jaw development and compare mutant mice to controls. This will be achieved through a combination of fluorescent labelling of bone, determining musculoskeletal anatomy and mapping molecular data to mechanical data retrieved via finite element modelling. 

 

The candidate will join a team of researchers in Bristol and at King’s London, who seek to understand the role of mechanics and development in determining the morphology, function and evolution of the mammalian jaw.

What will you be doing?

You will lead a research project and will be responsible for data collection and analysis. Specifically, this involves laboratory imaging with microCT and computational modelling. You will be responsible for liaising with the PI and collaborators, lead publications in international journals, present results at international conferences and contribute to public engagement and curate a deposit data.  

There is opportunity to help supervise PhD and MSc students and undergraduate summer interns working on the project, and where necessary, help organise scanning sessions, synchrotron beamtime applications, mouse colony management, and research visits.

You should apply if

We are looking for a candidate with the following Essential skills:

Experience of research on vertebrate skeletal or craniofacial development using mouse as an animal model
Experience of histology, fluorescent labelling, and imaging of bone
Knowledge of vertebrate craniofacial anatomy
Experience of transcriptomics: including spatial transcriptomics of skeletal tissue
A record of research outputs appropriate to career stage in subject relevant to this project
Ability to plan and manage own research to deadlines

 

It is also Desirable that the candidate possess:

Experience of working with transgenic or mutant mouse lines in a laboratory setting
Experience of microCT scanning

 

It is also Essential that the candidate possesses:

A PhD or near completion, or equivalent research experience in an academic, industrial or clinical setting equivalent to a PhD in developmental biology, skeletal biology, or a closely related field.

 

Desirable

UK Home Office personal licence (PIL), or equivalent training.

postings.advert_text:
Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 2 years in the first instance.

Applications are invited for a postdoctoral research position in the Theory of Condensed Matter group, Cavendish Laboratory, University of Cambridge, in the group of Prof. N.R. Cooper. The post is funded by the EPSRC Programme Grant "Quantum Advantage in Quantitative Quantum Simulation" (QQQS). The post is for a fixed term of 2 years, with an anticipated start date in autumn 2027.

The role holder will carry out theoretical research on quantum many-body systems, in close connection with experiments in analogue quantum simulation. Topics of current interest include: phase-space microscopy of quantum gases, as a probe of strongly correlated, topological and entangled states; the resilience of topological order to decoherence and measurement; collective light-matter coupling in arrays of quantum emitters, including in solid-state materials; and the quantum dynamics of nonlinear classical fields, such as false vacuum decay, quantised vortices and magnetic defects. Much of this work is carried out together with experimental partners within the programme, and the role holder will have opportunities to work closely with them. The role holder will work closely with Prof. Cooper and will be given significant opportunities to help set the research directions and to establish an independent research profile.

The successful candidate will hold (or be close to obtaining) a PhD in Physics or a closely related discipline, with expertise in the theory of quantum many-body systems and a track record of publishing scientific research. A solid command of analytical and/or computational methods is required. Research experience in one or more of the topics above, and a track record of collaboration with experimental groups, are desirable. The candidate will also have the ability to work within a team, and to present research background, techniques and results clearly and effectively.

Appointment at Research Associate is dependent on having a PhD, including those who have submitted but not yet received their PhD (in which case appointment will initially be made at Research Assistant and amended to Research Associate when the PhD is awarded).

Click the 'Apply' button below to register an account with our recruitment system (if you have not already) and apply online.

We are excited to launch this opportunity for a Research Associate to join the John Walton Muscular Dystrophy Research Centre at Newcastle University and contribute to an ambitious programme investigating the “dark proteome” in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD).

 

You will join an internationally recognised centre of excellence in neuromuscular disease research, working alongside clinicians, scientists and computational researchers. The project is delivered in collaboration with leading groups at the Human Technopole (HT) in Milan, Italy, and the University of Colorado Anschutz, USA.

 

The Project

 

The project aims to characterise the “dark proteome” in FSHD, focusing on previously unannotated or poorly characterised proteins arising from non-canonical translation. Using patient-derived skeletal muscle biopsies and complementary experimental systems, the team will generate and integrate proteomic, transcriptomic and clinical data to identify novel disease mechanisms, potential biomarkers and opportunities for therapeutic development.

 

The Role

 

The post holder will contribute to the generation, integration and biological interpretation of multi-omics datasets and their validation in cellular models of neuromuscular disease.

 

This is an excellent opportunity for a researcher looking to combine hands-on technical expertise with collaborative and translational research.

 

What we are looking for

 

We are looking for a researcher with experience in skeletal muscle biology and research in neuromuscular disorders. Experience with human tissues, transcriptomics, and proteomics would be advantageous. You will have experience developing or optimising experimental workflows, interpreting research data and working effectively within multidisciplinary teams.

 

Key information

 

This is a fixed-term post for 21 months with the potential for extension. The role will involve international travel to collaborate with project partners.

 

Flexible or part-time working may be considered where compatible with the project requirements.

 

We follow the Researcher Development Concordat and provide opportunities for mentoring, research planning, career development funding and support with research and innovation applications.

 

Further information and applications

 

The successful candidate will report to Giorgio Tasca, Clinical Professor of Neuromuscular Sciences. For an informal discussion about the role, please contact him at Giorgio.tasca@newcastle.ac.uk

 

Please note in order to commence the role you will require medical pre-screening.

 

Please submit a CV and covering letter, highlighting your relevant experience in sample analysis, omics research, experimental workflow development and collaborative, multi-site research.

We are seeking to appoint a Research Assistant to work in the laboratories of Prof Brendan Wren to use glycoengineering to develop enteric vaccines and novel glyco-diagnostics. The post-holder will join a research team of ten staff at the LSHTM and will have an opportunity to contribute to publications in high impact international scientific journals and be part of a wider consortium in UK.

The successful applicant will have a relevant first degree in the field of Medical Microbiology, relevant experience in Laboratory molecular biology & glycoengineering, relevant analytical skills in Glycoengineering/molecular biology. Further particulars are included in the job-description.

The post is fixed term until 30 June 2027 and full-time 35 hours per week, 1.0 FTE. The post is funded by EPSRC and is available from 01 January 2027. The salary will be on the LSHTM scale, Grade 5 in the range £40,784 - £46,643 per annum pro rata (inclusive of London Weighting). 

The post will be subject to the LSHTM terms and conditions of service. Annual leave entitlement is 30 working days per year, pro rata for part-time staff. In addition to this there are discretionary “Wellbeing Days”. Membership of the Pension Scheme is available. The post is based in Keppel Street, London at LSHTM.

Applications should be made on-line via our jobs website. Online applications will be accepted by the automated system until 10pm of the closing date. Any queries regarding the application process may be addressed to jobs@lshtm.ac.uk. Please quote reference ITD-DIB-2026-19-R.

The supporting statement section should set out how your qualifications, experience and training meet each of the selection criteria. Please provide one or more paragraphs addressing each criterion. The supporting statement is an essential part of the selection process and thus a failure to provide this information will mean that the application will not be considered. An answer to any of the criteria such as "Please see attached CV" will not be considered acceptable. 

Please note that if you are shortlisted and are unable to attend on the interview date it may not be possible to offer you an alternative date.
